archetypes.name: line-anchor-verifier
archetypes.rationale: The plan makes 10+ specific line-number claims (1045-1053, 1052, 1557, 1567, 139-147, 2262-2267, 280, 304, 173, 2333, 2365, 2465, 3805, 889-905) that directly govern which code gets edited; a single off-by-one misdirects the entire surgical fix.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/ship-pr.sh and verify that each line number cited in the plan actually contains the code the plan claims: the three unconditional trailing `set -e` sites (around lines 1052, 1557, 1567), the save/restore reference idiom at lines 139-147, the harness-invocation pair at lines 2262-2267, the `_RCC_CMD_RC` consumers at lines 280 and 304, the global default at line 173, and the `_run_per_job_command_once` callers at lines 2333, 2365, 2465. Also verify the plan's characterization of each site — e.g., that the trailing `set -e` at each claimed location is truly unconditional and not already inside a conditional guard. Flag any line-number drift or mischaracterized code. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: leak-scope-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan asserts exactly three unconditional set-e toggle sites need fixing; if other set+e/set-e pairs exist in the script with the same unconditional pattern, the fix is incomplete and the crash class survives under a different trigger path.
archetypes.prompt_body: Scan scripts/ship-pr.sh for every occurrence of `set +e` and `set -e` (or `set -eo`, `set -euo`, etc.) and determine whether any are unconditional trailing re-enables outside the three sites the plan identifies (the helper around line 1052 and the two pr-prep wrappers around lines 1557 and 1567). Also verify the plan's claim that `_run_per_job_command_once` is always called under an `if` test (lines 2333, 2365, 2465) and therefore is already errexit-safe without hardening. If additional unconditional `set -e` sites exist that could leak into other harness-capture calls, or if the `_run_per_job_command_once` exemption is wrong, the plan's scope is incomplete. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-harness-fit
archetypes.rationale: The test plan references specific existing infrastructure (section_runs gating, source guard at line 3805, pattern from lines 889-905, oos-disposition-gate stub path) that must actually exist and support the described approach; if the framework differs, the test section cannot be implemented as written.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/test-ship-pr.sh and verify that the infrastructure the plan relies on is present: the `section_runs` gating mechanism, the side-effect-free source guard cited at line 3805, and the existing source-witness test pattern at lines 889-905 that the new regression section is meant to mirror. Also verify that `skills/implement/scripts/oos-disposition-gate.sh` (or the resolved gate path called from the helper) exists at the path the plan assumes for stubbing. Check whether the plan's proposed test structure — calling the helper and the two pr-prep toggle paths directly under the source guard with minimal fixtures — is compatible with how those functions actually acquire their dependencies (STATE_FILE, IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR, write_state). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
